heading: INT. MUSEUM OF LOCKS - GREAT HALL - NIGHT

units.text: INT. MUSEUM OF LOCKS - GREAT HALL - NIGHT
A vaulted gallery lined with glass cabinets of antique locks, padlocks, and hand-wrought keys.
Gaslamp-style fixtures cast brass light.
A grandfather clock ticks.
Under a glass dome in the centre, an empty velvet cushion.
INSPECTOR AMBROSE TREVELYAN, fifties, in a bowler hat, walks the length of the hall with hands clasped behind him.
He pauses at the cushion.
The Duke's Key. Gone at half-past nine.
units.name: AMBROSE

units.text: LADY CORDELIA ASHGROVE, sixties, widow, in pearls and furs, sits stiffly on a bench.
DR. PERIKLES NAKOS, forties, curator, wrings his hands beside her.
MISS JOSEPHINE FINCH, twenties, the cataloguer, stands pale near the stairs.
MR. HADLEY, seventies, the night butler, holds a tray of untouched sherry.
It is an outrage.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: Madam, the cabinet was locked.
units.name: PERIKLES

units.text: Locked, yes. Opened, no.
units.name: AMBROSE

units.text: Then how--
units.name: JOSEPHINE

units.text: Miss Finch. You were the last to leave the hall.
units.name: AMBROSE

units.text: I was.
units.name: JOSEPHINE

units.text: You saw nothing?
units.name: AMBROSE

units.text: Only Mr. Hadley, with the sherry.
units.name: JOSEPHINE

units.text: I never left the pantry, sir.
units.name: HADLEY

units.text: That is a pity.
units.name: AMBROSE

units.text: Ambrose raises the glass dome, sets it aside, and picks up the velvet cushion.
He turns it over, examines the underside, and shakes it.
Dust falls.
Perikles and Cordelia lean away; Josephine and Hadley edge toward the door.
Nobody leave.
units.name: AMBROSE

units.text: They all freeze.
The clock ticks.
The key was never in the cabinet. It was swapped at the last catalogue. The one on this cushion was a copy.
units.name: AMBROSE

units.text: Preposterous.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: Dr. Nakos, who signed the catalogue?
units.name: AMBROSE

units.text: Perikles looks at Josephine.
Josephine looks at Hadley.
Hadley looks at Cordelia.
Cordelia rises, drawing her furs about her like a shield, and takes one step toward the stairs.
The four of them bolt in four directions.
Ambrose lifts a whistle to his lips and blows.
Doors slam.
Footsteps thunder on marble.
A constable's lantern swings through the arch, and the hall fills with shouting.
